newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine graft impeding foreign investment - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Argentine graft impeding foreign investment - WSJ.

text.p: Corruption in Argentina is eroding foreign investor confidence and impeding the arrival of international funds, Edward Schumacher, director of The Wall Street Journal Americas, said Thursday.
"Argentina is a model among emerging markets...but abroad it has a poor image because of cases of corruption. If there's no confidence, then there are limits on investment," Schumacher said
He was speaking at a seminar called "Argentina in the eyes of Wall Street" organized by the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.
Schumacher said the ouster of former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo almost one year ago proved there are many economists in the country capable of leading current policy.
However, "There's still a lot to do," he said. "Foreign investors are tempted to pray that (President Carlos) Menem returns in 1999."
Nevertheless, he admitted a change of president would be healthy for democracy.

Schumacher described ties between Argentina and the United States as very good, although he said the upcoming October visit of U.S. President Bill Clinton could be postponed for reasons he did not disclose.
